<file path="infra/terraform/modules/worker/main.tf">
# Same image as the API, no load balancer. Pulls signing jobs from SQS (large files, batch signing, cert generation).
# The app switches behaviour on WORKER_MODE=true (or set `command` to run a different entrypoint).
variable "name" { type = string }
variable "region" { type = string }
variable "cluster_arn" { type = string }
variable "cluster_name" { type = string }
variable "subnet_ids" { type = list(string) }
variable "security_group_id" { type = string }
variable "ecr_repository_url" { type = string }
variable "execution_role_arn" { type = string }
variable "task_role_arn" { type = string }
variable "log_group_name" { type = string }
variable "container_environment" { type = map(string) }
variable "container_secrets" { type = list(map(string)) }
variable "image_tag" {
  type    = string
  default = "bootstrap"
}
variable "command" {
  type    = list(string)
  default = []
}
variable "cpu_architecture" {
  type    = string
  default = "ARM64"
}
variable "cpu" {
  type    = number
  default = 1024
}
variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}
variable "desired_count" {
  type    = number
  default = 1
}
variable "min_count" {
  type    = number
  default = 1
}
variable "max_count" {
  type    = number
  default = 5
}

resource "aws_ecs_task_definition" "worker" {
  family                   = "${var.name}-worker"
  requires_compatibilities = ["FARGATE"]
  network_mode             = "awsvpc"
  cpu                      = var.cpu
  memory                   = var.memory
  execution_role_arn       = var.execution_role_arn
  task_role_arn            = var.task_role_arn

  runtime_platform {
    operating_system_family = "LINUX"
    cpu_architecture        = var.cpu_architecture
  }

  volume { name = "scratch" }

  container_definitions = jsonencode([merge({
    name                   = "worker"
    image                  = "${var.ecr_repository_url}:${var.image_tag}"
    essential              = true
    readonlyRootFilesystem = true
    stopTimeout            = 120 # let in-flight signing jobs finish on scale-in / deploy
    mountPoints            = [{ sourceVolume = "scratch", containerPath = "/tmp", readOnly = false }]
    linuxParameters = {
      initProcessEnabled = true
      capabilities       = { drop = ["ALL"] }
    }
    environment = [for k, v in merge(var.container_environment, { WORKER_MODE = "true" }) : { name = k, value = v }]
    secrets     = var.container_secrets
    logConfiguration = {
      logDriver = "awslogs"
      options = {
        awslogs-group         = var.log_group_name
        awslogs-region        = var.region
        awslogs-stream-prefix = "worker"
      }
    }
  }, length(var.command) > 0 ? { command = var.command } : {})])
}

resource "aws_ecs_service" "worker" {
  name                               = "worker"
  cluster                            = var.cluster_arn
  task_definition                    = aws_ecs_task_definition.worker.arn
  desired_count                      = var.desired_count
  launch_type                        = "FARGATE"
  deployment_minimum_healthy_percent = 100
  deployment_maximum_percent         = 200

  deployment_circuit_breaker {
    enable   = true
    rollback = true
  }

  network_configuration {
    subnets          = var.subnet_ids
    security_groups  = [var.security_group_id]
    assign_public_ip = false
  }

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [task_definition, desired_count]
  }
}

resource "aws_appautoscaling_target" "worker" {
  service_namespace  = "ecs"
  scalable_dimension = "ecs:service:DesiredCount"
  resource_id        = "service/${var.cluster_name}/${aws_ecs_service.worker.name}"
  min_capacity       = var.min_count
  max_capacity       = var.max_count
}

resource "aws_appautoscaling_policy" "cpu" {
  name               = "${var.name}-worker-cpu"
  policy_type        = "TargetTrackingScaling"
  service_namespace  = aws_appautoscaling_target.worker.service_namespace
  scalable_dimension = aws_appautoscaling_target.worker.scalable_dimension
  resource_id        = aws_appautoscaling_target.worker.resource_id

  target_tracking_scaling_policy_configuration {
    target_value       = 60
    scale_in_cooldown  = 300
    scale_out_cooldown = 60
    predefined_metric_specification {
      predefined_metric_type = "ECSServiceAverageCPUUtilization"
    }
  }
}

output "service_name" { value = aws_ecs_service.worker.name }
output "service_arn" { value = aws_ecs_service.worker.id }
output "task_family" { value = aws_ecs_task_definition.worker.family }
</file>

<file path="infra/README.md">
# Infrastructure

Terraform for the signing/PKI SaaS on AWS. Dev and prod should be **separate AWS accounts**; each uses its own state key.

```
Browser ─▶ CloudFront (+WAF, TLS) ─┬─ /*      ─▶ S3 (SPA, private, OAC)
                                   └─ /api/*  ─▶ API Gateway HTTP API (Cognito JWT, throttling)
                                                   └─ VPC link ─▶ internal ALB ─▶ ECS Fargate (private subnets)
                                                                                   ├─▶ Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 (data subnets)
                                                                                   ├─▶ KMS keywrap key (envelope-encrypts customer private keys)
                                                                                   └─▶ S3 documents bucket (presigned upload/download, KMS)
Auth: Cognito user pool (identity only). Orgs / invitations / roles live in the app DB.

Async:   API ─▶ SQS jobs queue (+DLQ, KMS) ─▶ ECS "worker" service (same image, WORKER_MODE=true)
Email:   SES domain identity (DKIM) + configuration set, used for invitations
Audit:   CloudTrail (mgmt events incl. every KMS call + S3 data events on documents) + GuardDuty   [enable_account_security]
Alerts:  CloudWatch alarms -> SNS -> e-mail; monthly AWS Budget
```

## First-time setup

```bash
# 1. Per account: state bucket + GitHub OIDC provider
cd infra/terraform/bootstrap
terraform init && terraform apply \
  -var state_bucket_name=<unique-name> -var github_repo=<owner/repo> -var infra_environment=dev-infra   # prod-infra in the prod account

# 2. Fill in app/envs/<env>.backend.hcl and <env>.tfvars (REPLACE markers)

# 3. ECR must exist before the first image can be pushed
cd ../app
terraform init -backend-config=envs/dev.backend.hcl
terraform apply -var-file=envs/dev.tfvars -target=module.compute.aws_ecr_repository.api

# 4. Build + push the API image (tag "bootstrap" matches api_image_tag) for the same CPU arch as api_cpu_architecture
# 5. Full apply
terraform apply -var-file=envs/dev.tfvars
```

Switching environment: `terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=envs/prod.backend.hcl` and use `envs/prod.tfvars`
(with credentials for the prod account).

## GitHub configuration

Create four GitHub **environments**: `dev`, `prod` (app deploys), `dev-infra`, `prod-infra` (terraform apply).
Put required reviewers on `prod` and `prod-infra`.

| Where                          | Name                                                                                                              | Value (source)                                              |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| env `dev-infra` / `prod-infra` | `TF_APPLY_ROLE_ARN`                                                                                               | bootstrap output `terraform_apply_role_arn` of that account |
| repo variables                 | `DEV_TF_PLAN_ROLE_ARN`, `PROD_TF_PLAN_ROLE_ARN`                                                                   | bootstrap output `terraform_plan_role_arn`                  |
| env `dev` / `prod`             | `AWS_REGION`, `DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`                                                                                   | `github_deploy_role_arn`                                    |
| env `dev` / `prod`             | `ECR_REPOSITORY_URL`, `ECS_CLUSTER`, `SITE_BUCKET`, `CF_DISTRIBUTION_ID`, `API_TASK_FAMILY`, `WORKER_TASK_FAMILY` | matching `terraform output` values                          |

Run `terraform fmt -recursive infra/terraform` once before opening the first PR (the plan job enforces `fmt -check`).

## Contract with the application

Env vars injected into the container: `PORT, AWS_REGION, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD,
DOCUMENTS_BUCKET, KEYWRAP_KMS_KEY_ID, COGNITO_ISSUER, COGNITO_CLIENT_ID, GNUPGHOME, JOBS_QUEUE_URL`,
plus `SES_FROM_DOMAIN, SES_CONFIGURATION_SET` when `email_domain` is set, and `WORKER_MODE=true` in the worker only.

- Worker: long-poll `JOBS_QUEUE_URL`, delete the message only after the result is persisted, and handle SIGTERM
  (tasks get 120 s to drain). Jobs must be idempotent: messages move to the DLQ after 5 failed receives.
- Health check: `GET /api/health` -> 200 (unauthenticated). All other `/api/**` require a Cognito JWT.
- Read-only root filesystem: write only to `/tmp`.
- Every KMS keywrap call **must** pass an EncryptionContext (IAM enforces it), e.g. `{org_id, key_id}`.

## Workflows (`.github/workflows`)

- `infra.yml`: PR -> `fmt/validate/plan` for dev and prod (read-only role, plan posted as a PR comment). Merge to main -> apply dev, then apply prod after approval.
- `deploy.yml` / `_deploy.yml`: merge to main -> dev, then prod after approval: build arm64 image -> push -> register new task definitions for `api` and `worker` -> wait for stable -> build SPA -> sync to S3 -> invalidate `index.html`.
- `ci.yml`: PR checks for `apps/**`.
  All use GitHub OIDC; the deploy role is scoped to ECR push, ECS update, the SPA bucket, and one CloudFront invalidation.
  Terraform ignores `task_definition` and `desired_count` on the service, so infra applies never roll back a deploy.

## Still not included (recommended next)

AWS Config / Security Hub, AWS Backup with cross-region copy, multi-region DR, DB migration task + workflow step, a CloudWatch dashboard,
WAF in front of the API Gateway URL (it is reachable directly, bypassing CloudFront), Cognito custom domain, per-tenant S3 prefixes
with IAM session policies, and a split of the API and worker task roles (the worker currently shares the API role).
</file>

<file path="ROADMAP.md">
# POC Plan: AI Certificate Management on AWS

The key to a good POC is a **narrow vertical slice**: prove the riskiest, most valuable idea end to end rather than building every feature shallowly. Here, that is "AI-driven policy enforcement over certificate lifecycle, with access control."

## **<!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c1 -->**1\. Define scope and success criteria (Week 1\)

- **Hypothesis:** AI can safely automate certificate and secret management tasks that are normally manual.
- **In scope:** certificate issuance and renewal, role-based access control, one policy enforced by AI, an audit trail.
- **Out of scope (for now):** multi-tenant billing, full UI, every integration, HA and DR.
- **Success metrics:** e.g. certificate issued in under 1 minute, 100% of actions logged, AI correctly translates 9 of 10 test policies, zero unauthorized access in tests.<!-- gdoc_comment_end: c1 -->

## 2\. Choose the architecture and AWS services \- **עמית**

| Capability                           | Suggested service                                          |
| :----------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------- |
| Certificate issuance                 | AWS Private CA \+ ACM                                      |
| Keyrings / encryption keys           | AWS KMS                                                    |
| Password generation / secret storage | Secrets Manager (+ Lambda generator)                       |
| Access control                       | IAM, Cognito, Amazon Verified Permissions (Cedar policies) |
| API layer                            | API Gateway \+ Lambda                                      |
| Data                                 | DynamoDB (inventory, policies), S3 (reports)               |
| Automation                           | EventBridge \+ Step Functions                              |
| Audit                                | CloudTrail, CloudWatch, AWS Config                         |
| AI features                          | Amazon Bedrock (with Guardrails, optionally Agents)        |

&nbsp;

Use the two AWS reference architectures as guides for isolation, encryption, and compliance patterns, and reuse their ideas for separating sensitive data and logging:

&nbsp;

- [Data Escrow Environment](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/reference-architecture-diagrams/latest/data-escrow-environment/data-escrow-environment.html)
- [Content Moderation and Compliance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/reference-architecture-diagrams/latest/content-moderation-compliance/content-moderation-compliance.html)

## 3\. Build the foundation (Week 1-2) \- **דולב**

- Create a dedicated sandbox AWS account (never use production).
- Define everything as code with CDK or Terraform.
- Set up a VPC, KMS customer-managed keys, CloudTrail, and a least-privilege IAM baseline.

## 4\. Build the core certificate service (Week 2\) \- **איתי**

- Stand up a Private CA.
- Create API endpoints: `request-cert`, `renew-cert`, `revoke-cert`, `list-certs`.
- Store certificate metadata (owner, expiry, status) in DynamoDB.
- Add an EventBridge rule that detects upcoming expirations and triggers automatic renewal via Step Functions.

## 5\. Add access control (Week 2-3) \- **דן**

- Authenticate users with Cognito.
- Define roles (admin, team owner, auditor) and write Cedar policies in Verified Permissions.
- Enforce authorization in every API call, and test that unauthorized requests are denied.

## <!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c2 -->6\. Add keyring and password features (Week 3\)<!-- gdoc_comment_end: c2 -->

- Lambda generates passwords following a configurable policy (length, complexity, rotation period).
- Store them in Secrets Manager with automatic rotation.
- Keep this minimal: one secret type is enough for the POC.

## <!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c3 -->7\. Add the AI layer (Week 3-4)<!-- gdoc_comment_end: c3 -->

This is the differentiator, so pick two or three focused use cases:

&nbsp;

- **Natural language to policy:** an admin types "All production certs must expire within 90 days and use RSA 3072+," and Bedrock generates a Cedar or config rule that is shown for human approval before activation.
- **Anomaly detection:** Bedrock analyzes CloudTrail logs and flags unusual patterns, like a burst of certificate requests at 3 AM.
- **Compliance assistant:** answers questions like "Which certificates violate our policy?" using your inventory.

&nbsp;

**Important guardrails:** use Bedrock Guardrails, require human approval for any destructive or permission-changing action, validate all AI output against a schema, and never give the model direct access to private keys or secret values.

## 8\. Build one integration (Week 4\)

Show automated enrollment with something simple: a webhook or API call from a CI/CD pipeline or a sample EC2/ECS app that requests and installs a certificate automatically.

## 9\. Add a minimal interface (Week 4-5)

A simple dashboard (S3 \+ CloudFront or Amplify) showing the certificate inventory, policy status, and audit log is enough. A CLI or Postman collection is fine too.

## <!-- gdoc_comment_begin: c4 -->10\. Test and validate (Week 5\)

- Functional tests for each flow.
- Security tests: attempt privilege escalation, prompt injection against the AI features, and access to another team's resources.
- Measure against your success metrics from step 1\.<!-- gdoc_comment_end: c4 -->

## 11\. Demo, document, and decide (Week 6\)

- Record a demo of the full flow: request, approval, issuance, auto-renewal, and AI policy creation.
- Document the architecture, cost per operation (Bedrock and Private CA costs add up quickly), limitations, and risks.
- Write a go / no-go recommendation with a roadmap for the production build.

## Cost tips

AWS Private CA has a notable monthly fee per CA, so delete it when not demoing. Set AWS Budgets alerts and use small Bedrock models while iterating.

&nbsp;

---
